---
title: MCP server
description: Give a coding agent Teire's scan and catalog, so it checks the repository it is editing and looks up a provider's deprecations before it writes code against them.
icon: Plug
---

`teire mcp` serves Teire's tools over stdio. The protocol uses stdout, and logs go to stderr.

<Tabs items={["Claude Code", "Other clients"]}>
<Tab value="Claude Code">

```bash
claude mcp add teire -- npx -y teire-cli mcp
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Other clients">

Cursor, Windsurf and other clients take the same command in their MCP config:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "teire": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "teire-cli", "mcp"] } } }
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Tools

| Tool | Input | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `scan_path` | `path`, optional `fresh` | The scan as JSON: ecosystems, providers, groups of findings with their sites, and notes. Results are cached 5 minutes per path, unless `fresh` |
| `explain_finding` | `path`, `key` (a group key, change ID or package name) | The finding group with every call site and its change records: the computed API diff for a package, or the provider's quoted notice |
| `list_changes` | optional `provider`, `ecosystem`, `kind`, `subject` | Changes from the public catalog: ID, title, kind, class, date and replacement |
| `get_change` | `id` | One full change record |

Every tool is marked read-only. None of them writes to the repository or to GitHub.

## What an agent does with it

- **Before an upgrade:** call `scan_path` on the repository, then `explain_finding` on what it reports. The agent gets the lines to change and the change record: the computed API diff for a package, or the provider's quoted notice for a model or API change.
- **Before writing model code:** call `list_changes` with `provider: "openai"` (or any provider) to see which model IDs are retired or retiring, and what replaces them.
- **In review:** call `get_change` on an ID from a Teire PR for the full record.
